How many rounds does the rotating update need?

For the same 128-bit inverse construction with a 16-bit update, 10 rounds are necessary and 36 suffice for the worst ordered quadruple at total variation (TV) distance 2−1282^{-128}. The previous two-sweep analysis certified 81 rounds. The upper bound of 36 also holds for every degree-15 control polynomial with the same geometry. All statements assume fresh independent uniform XOR keys shared by the inputs. Definitions and 10-round lower bound · Polynomial construction

What a single update can retain

Write N=2nN=2^n, B=2bB=2^b, Q=N/BQ=N/B, d=⌈n/b⌉d=\lceil n/b\rceil and p=(t2)p=\binom t2. In a rotating frame each layer updates one window of bb bits. A sweep of dd windows covers the word. An ideal layer chooses a fresh independent uniform offset for each distinct control (the other n−bn-b bits). The actual layer applies f(z+u)f(z+u) to each control zz with one common uniform uu. Let β\beta bound every nontrivial parity of relative offsets on at most s=min(t,Q)s=\min(t,Q) distinct controls. For the inverse one can use [2(s−1)Q+s+1]/Q[2(s-1)\sqrt Q+s+1]/Q. For a degree-15 control polynomial at t≤4t\le4 one can use 12/Q12/\sqrt Q. Write β2\beta_2 for the corresponding pair bound. The public cipher after rr rounds has exactly the TV distance of its relative differences after r−1r-1 such layers. Character estimates and final-mask identity · Degree-15 bound

A short warmup before one sweep

Track a pair in an ideal layer. If both controls agree, its nonzero window difference stays fixed. Otherwise the written difference is uniform among BB possibilities. Thus, conditional on any history, a write is zero with probability at most 1/B1/B. To collide on the next control, the pair must agree on each of the previous mm written windows, provided those windows and the new window are mutually disjoint. Their successive writes must all have been zero, an event of probability at most B−mB^{-m}. This reasoning applies up to m=c=⌊n/b⌋−1m=c=\lfloor n/b\rfloor-1 even when the last window of a sweep overlaps the first.

Use kk warmup layers and then one full sweep. During the final dd layers, couple the ideal process to a process that always uses independent offsets for each label. The latter process ends with independent uniform words. The coupling agrees until two labels share a control. The ideal process is distinct-valued, so conditioning the independent target on distinctness decreases TV. A union bound gives ek=p∑j=0d−1B−min(k+j,c). e_k=p\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}B^{-\min(k+j,c)}.

At every history, relative writes in the real layer have chi-squared divergence at most v=(Bs−1−1)β2v=(B^{s-1}-1)\beta^2 from the ideal writes, by Parseval. Thus the second moment of their likelihood ratio is at most 1+v1+v. Multiplying the successive likelihood ratios and conditioning step by step gives a path second moment at most (1+v)d+k(1+v)^{d+k}. TV of the endpoint is at most half the square root of the resulting chi-squared divergence. If a supplied permutation table differs from the specified construction at hh entries, successive coupling contributes at most (d+k)th/N(d+k)th/N. Therefore a block of d+kd+k difference layers has worst row TV at most δk=ek+12(1+v)d+k−1+(d+k)th/N. \delta_k=e_k+\tfrac12\sqrt{(1+v)^{d+k}-1}+(d+k)th/N.

A kernel with worst row TV δk\delta_k from stationarity contracts signed zero-mass measures in TV by at most 2δk2\delta_k. A sequence of blocks yields TV at most 12∏i(2δki)\tfrac12\prod_i(2\delta_{k_i}). The program compares products for different warmup lengths by dynamic programming with upward rounding. At 128 bits, 16-bit updates and four inputs, five ten-layer blocks plus the final full mask give 51 rounds for either control family. The next argument exploits more information about which starting tuples retain a difference.

A sweep as an operator

Assume bb divides nn and use the specified permutation (h=0h=0). Every coordinate is then written exactly once per sweep. Work on full ordered distinct tuples with uniform law UU. In the real translated layers, add an independent uniform common bb-bit offset to the updated window. This leaves the one-step transition on differences unchanged. Earlier common shifts only translate the input to the next uniform mask. Each lifted layer is a mixture of bijections on the entire word, so UU is stationary. Upper bounds on its full-tuple TV give upper bounds on difference TV by projection.

Let IjI_j and MjM_j denote the ideal and lifted real kernels for one window. Fix the controls of the tuple and all within-control differences. If there are ll distinct controls, the remaining degrees of freedom are one anchor window value per control, forming the additive group of ll blocks. The real update is convolution on this group. The ideal update averages uniformly. Fourier characters are an orthonormal eigenbasis for the difference of these two kernels. Characters sensitive to a common offset have zero mean in both processes. For the remaining nonconstant characters the real expectation is at most β\beta in absolute value. Hence ‖Mj−Ij‖2→2≤β\lVert M_j-I_j\rVert_{2\to2}\le\beta on each fiber and on their disjoint union with uniform measure. Telescoping the product over one sweep costs at most dβd\beta, because all kernels are contractions in L2(U)L^2(U).

Let KK be one complete ideal sweep and JJ projection to uniform. A starting tuple xx and ending tuple yy specify all the intermediate states: at every step, read the processed prefix from yy and the remaining suffix from xx. For a compatible path let ljl_j be the number of distinct controls at step jj, and put D=∑j=1d(t−lj)D=\sum_{j=1}^d(t-l_j). Its ideal transition probability is B−dt+DB^{-dt+D}. Thus K(x,y)/U(y)≤BDK(x,y)/U(y)\le B^D since (N)t≤Nt(N)_t\le N^t.

Make a graph on the tt labels, joining pairs that collide on some control during this sweep. Two labels in the same control group have distinct window values. They retain this nonzero difference, so they can collide at most once in a sweep of disjoint windows. Each group of mm labels accounts for m−1m-1 units of DD and (m2)\binom m2 pair collisions. Hence DD is at most the graph's number of edges. A graph of rank vv (number of vertices minus number of connected components) has at most (v+12)\binom{v+1}2 edges.

Draw XX from UU, independently of all the random switch tables. Fix the switch tables for the sweep. To realize any prescribed set of vv forest edges with specified collision times, expose the starting labels along the forest from its roots. When adding a child, its parent position at the specified time fixes the required control. The maps from starting words to words at that time are bijective. The child's starting word is uniform among at least N−t+1N-t+1 unused words, and at most B−1B-1 of them can match its parent's control. Union over at most (pv)\binom pv forests and dvd^v time choices. Since a rank-vv graph contains such a forest, S=∑v=1t−1(pv)(d(B−1)N−t+1)vB(v+12)bounds𝔼[BD−1]. S=\sum_{v=1}^{t-1}\binom pv \left(\frac{d(B-1)}{N-t+1}\right)^v B^{\binom{v+1}{2}} \quad\text{bounds}\quad \mathbb E[B^D-1]. The squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm of K−JK-J is 𝔼[K(X,Y)/U(Y)]−1\mathbb E[K(X,Y)/U(Y)]-1 for X∼U,Y∼K(X,⋅)X\sim U,\ Y\sim K(X,\cdot). Therefore ‖K−J‖2→2≤S\lVert K-J\rVert_{2\to2}\le\sqrt S. The lifted real sweep contracts mean-zero L2(U)L^2(U) by at most σ=S+dβ\sigma=\sqrt S+d\beta. The adjoint has the same norm, which is the direction required for evolving densities.

From a fixed starting tuple

For one actual lifted sweep, a compatible path has density relative to UU at most ABDA B^D with A=[1+(Bt−1−1)β]dA=[1+(B^{t-1}-1)\beta]^d. To see this, Fourier inversion on the lj−1l_j-1 relative offsets bounds the probability of any particular relative write by [1+(Blj−1−1)β]/Blj−1[1+(B^{l_j-1}-1)\beta]/B^{l_j-1}. The extra common offset supplies the independent uniform absolute anchor. Multiplying over the unique path gives the claim.

There is a useful deterministic bound on DD. Choose one of the tt labels uniformly and follow its written prefix. The increase in prefix entropy at step jj is the entropy of the new window conditioned on the old prefix. Conditioning further on the control (old prefix and unwritten suffix) can only decrease that entropy. Within a control class of size mm, all mm new window values are distinct, giving log2m\log_2 m bits. Since mlog2m≥2(m−1)m\log_2 m\ge2(m-1) for integer m≥1m\ge1, the total increase that step is at least 2(t−lj)/t2(t-l_j)/t. The final prefix has entropy log2t\log_2 t. Thus D≤E=⌊tlog2(t)/2⌋D\le E=\lfloor t\log_2(t)/2\rfloor. If only the first window collides then D≤t−1D\le t-1.

For real writes the chance that a particular pair writes zero, conditional on any past, is at most a=1/B+(1−1/B)β2a=1/B+(1-1/B)\beta_2 by single-window Fourier inversion. A forced pair has probability zero of writing zero. After kk warmup layers the first window of the full sweep has some control collision with probability at most p0=min(1,pak)p_0=\min(1,p a^k), for 0≤k≤d−10\le k\le d-1. The chance of a later collision in that sweep is at most p1=min(1,p∑j=1d−1amin(k+j,d−1))p_1=\min(1,p\sum_{j=1}^{d-1} a^{\min(k+j,d-1)}). Conditioning on the state at the end of the warmup, the chi-squared divergence plus one of the sweep's output equals the expected transition density relative to UU. Convexity of divergence permits averaging that estimate over the warmup. Classifying paths by the first or a later collision gives H=Amin{BE,1+(Bt−1−1)p0+(BE−1)p1}−1 H=A\min\{B^E,1+(B^{t-1}-1)p_0+(B^E-1)p_1\}-1 as an upper bound on chi-squared divergence after the first k+dk+d layers. After another mm sweeps, TV is at most 12Hσm\tfrac12\sqrt H\,\sigma^m, at 1+k+d+md1+k+d+md cipher rounds.

For the 128-bit inverse with b=16,t=4b=16,t=4, the stationary contraction satisfies σ<2.53×10−14\sigma<2.53\times10^{-14}. With k=3k=3, three further sweeps give TV below 2−1342^{-134}. The degree-15 bound gives TV below 2−1342^{-134} with the same schedule. These are sufficient guarantees for every initial quadruple. They do not determine its exact mixing time.

Morris, Rogaway and Stegers analyze ordered inputs under the independent-switch Thorp shuffle. Gelman and Ta-Shma prove a bound for unordered sets under the Beneš switching network. The local character estimates used here also have published sources. The warmup estimate, forest count and application of the sweep norm to these explicit permutations are project derivations.
